newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE coffee nudges lower in sleepy AM trade.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE coffee nudges lower in sleepy AM trade.

text.p: Robusta coffee futures were lower and near session lows after a sleepy Wednesday morning trade with values kept down by overhead hedge selling notably from the Far East.

Indonesian sellers were making a comeback, selling into any price rise after much hesitation in the past weeks. The September futures prices had risen by some $192 in a week to an intraday high of $1,669 on Tuesday
But overall conditions were quiet and prices are likely to meander in a broad range between $1,600 and just below $1,700.
Traders said there was also not much left to do on spot July, which goes off the board at lunchtime on Thursday.
The uncovered position on July fell 114 lots to 161 at the close of business on Tuesday.
September gapped $13 down at the open and was driven to a session low of $1,640 per tonne. It finished the morning $24 down at $1,644.
Sept/Nov switches were traded at $8 this morning.
Turnover totalled 1,124 lots at the midsession.

Traders called the New York market to open slightly lower on numbers basis London. But they noted the underlying sentiment in arabicas remained bullish due to the tight availability of deliverable coffee in September.

"Concern so far about an arabica shortage in September is now established in prices for the moment and the market needs fresh news on the fundamental side to underpin recent technical gains," broker GNI said.
